header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from the fetched source documents; sha256 (when filled) is of the canonical body. Brackets and standard deductions are from Form IT-2105-I (2026), Instructions for Estimated Tax ('New York State tax rates' and the standard deduction table); cross-checked against Tax Foundation 2026. Starting point is federal AGI with New York additions/subtractions (NYAGI). There is no personal exemption for the filer or spouse; dependents get $1,000 each. Social Security included in federal AGI is fully subtracted. Pension/annuity exclusion: up to $20,000 per person age 59.5+ (each spouse has a separate $20,000 limit; unused amounts cannot be shared) for private pensions, annuities and IRA distributions; New York State/local and federal government pensions are fully exempt regardless of age. NOT modeled - tax benefit recapture: once NYAGI exceeds $107,650 the benefit of the lower brackets is progressively recaptured (IT-2105-I worksheets), so at high incomes tax approaches a flat rate on all taxable income. Itemized deductions are limited above $100,000 NYAGI. Local taxes not included: New York City resident tax 3.078% / 3.762% / 3.819% / 3.876% (bracket tops: single/MFS $12,000 / $25,000 / $50,000; MFJ $21,600 / $45,000 / $90,000; HOH $14,400 / $30,000 / $60,000), Yonkers resident surcharge, and MCTMT on self-employment earnings in the MTA district. The 10.3% and 10.9% brackets are temporary under current law. Brackets and deductions are not inflation-indexed.

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: $20,000 per person at 59.5 applies to private pensions/IRA/annuity income; NY and federal government pensions are fully exempt at any age
flags.brackets: tax benefit recapture above $107,650 NYAGI not modeled (understates tax for high incomes)
